claim: The atypical cadherins Fat and Dachsous (Ds) underlie planar cell polarity (PCP) in many tissues.
source: The atypical cadherins Fat and Dachsous (Ds) have been found to underlie planar cell polarity (PCP) in many tissues.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known finding from prior research.

claim: Theoretical models suggest that polarity can arise from localized feedbacks on Fat-Ds complexes at the cell boundary.
source: Theoretical models suggest that polarity can arise from localized feedbacks on Fat-Ds complexes at the cell boundary.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a prediction from theoretical models.

claim: There is currently no direct evidence for the existence or mechanism of localized feedbacks on Fat-Ds complexes.
source: However, there is currently no direct evidence for the existence or mechanism of such feedbacks.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a gap in current knowledge.

claim: Fat4-Ds1 complexes accumulate on cell boundaries in a threshold-like manner.
source: We show that Fat4-Ds1 complexes accumulate on cell boundaries in a threshold-like manner and exhibit dramatically slower dynamics than unbound Fat4 and Ds1.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Fat4-Ds1 complexes exhibit dramatically slower dynamics than unbound Fat4 and Ds1.
source: We show that Fat4-Ds1 complexes accumulate on cell boundaries in a threshold-like manner and exhibit dramatically slower dynamics than unbound Fat4 and Ds1.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by FRAP data in Figure 4.

claim: The slower dynamics of Fat4-Ds1 complexes suggests a localized feedback mechanism based on enhanced stability of Fat4-Ds1 complexes.
source: This suggests a localized feedback mechanism based on enhanced stability of Fat4-Ds1 complexes.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the FRAP data presented in Figure 4.

claim: Co-expression of Fat4 and Ds1 in the same cells is sufficient to induce polarization of Fat4-Ds1 complexes.
source: We also show that co-expression of Fat4 and Ds1 in the same cells is sufficient to induce polarization of Fat4-Ds1 complexes.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: Localized feedbacks on Fat4-Ds1 complexes can give rise to PCP.
source: Together, these results provide direct evidence that localized feedbacks on Fat4-Ds1 complexes can give rise to PCP.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study stated in the abstract.

claim: PCP defines the coordinated polarization of cells in the plane of a tissue.
source: Planar cell polarity (PCP) defines the coordinated polarization of cells in the plane of a tissue (Adler, 2002; Lewis and Davies, 2002; Lawrence et al., 2007; Wang and Nathans, 2007; Goodrich and Strutt, 2011)
evidence: This is a definition supported by multiple citations.

claim: PCP underlies the organization and geometry required for the proper function of many developing organs.
source: and underlies the organization and geometry required for the proper function of many developing organs.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: PCP is usually manifested by orientation of external structures, such as trichomes and sensory hair cells in Drosophila.
source: PCP is usually manifested by orientation of external structures, such as trichomes and sensory hair cells in Drosophila (Goodrich and Strutt, 2011; Strutt and Strutt, 2009)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: PCP is manifested by hair structures in the inner ear and skin of vertebrates.
source: and hair structures in the inner ear and skin of vertebrates (Montcouquiol et al., 2003; Dabdoub and Kelley, 2005; Saburi et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: At the molecular level, PCP is defined by asymmetric distribution of transmembrane protein complexes which belong to two families - the Frizzled/Van-Gogh pathway and the Fat/Dachsous pathway.
source: At the molecular level, PCP is defined by asymmetric distribution of transmembrane protein complexes which belong to two families - the Frizzled/Van-Gogh pathway (termed the 'core' pathway) and the Fat/Dachsous (Ft/Ds) pathway.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Both the Frizzled/Van-Gogh pathway and the Fat/Dachsous pathway were discovered in Drosophila but are conserved in higher vertebrates.
source: Both were discovered in Drosophila but are conserved in higher vertebrates (Goodrich and Strutt, 2011; Singh and Mlodzik, 2012; Sharma and McNeill, 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The main players in the Ft/Ds pathway in Drosophila are the large atypical cadherins Ft, Ds and the Golgi protein kinase Four-jointed (Fj).
source: The main players in the Ft/Ds pathway in Drosophila are the large atypical cadherins Ft, Ds and the Golgi protein kinase Four-jointed (Fj).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Ft and Ds take part in heterophilic interactions resulting in trans-hetero-complexes on the boundary between cells.
source: Ft and Ds take part in heterophilic interactions resulting in trans-hetero-complexes on the boundary between cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: There is no evidence of homophilic complexes of either Ft or Ds forming across cells.
source: Unlike for classical cadherins, there is no evidence of homophilic complexes of either Ft or Ds forming across cells (Matakatsu and Blair, 2004; Matis and Axelrod, 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The mammalian homologues of Ft and Ds include Fat1-4 and Ds1-2.
source: The mammalian homologues of Ft and Ds include Fat1-4 and Ds1-2.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Fat4 and Ds1 have the highest homology to Drosophila Ft and Ds.
source: However, Fat4 and Ds1 have the highest homology to Drosophila Ft and Ds, are the most widely expressed, and have the strongest knockout phenotypes (Rock et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Fat4 and Ds1 are the most widely expressed mammalian homologues of Drosophila Ft and Ds.
source: However, Fat4 and Ds1 have the highest homology to Drosophila Ft and Ds, are the most widely expressed, and have the strongest knockout phenotypes (Rock et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Fat4 and Ds1 have the strongest knockout phenotypes among mammalian homologues of Drosophila Ft and Ds.
source: However, Fat4 and Ds1 have the highest homology to Drosophila Ft and Ds, are the most widely expressed, and have the strongest knockout phenotypes (Rock et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Fat4 and Ds1 null mice show complex morphological abnormalities in the inner ear, kidney, brain, bone, lymph node, and more.
source: Fat4 and Ds1 null mice show complex morphological abnormalities in the inner ear, kidney, brain, bone, lymph node, and more. (Saburi et al., 2008; Ishiuchi et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: In humans, mutations in Fat4 and Ds1 were recently linked to various cancers and abnormal brain development.
source: In humans, mutations in Fat4 and Ds1 were recently linked to various cancers and abnormal brain development (Katoh, 2012; Cappello et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Polarized distributions of Fat4 and Ds1 in vertebrates have not been observed yet, probably due to lack of good reagents for staining these proteins in vivo.
source: Unlike in Drosophila, polarized distributions of Fat4 and Ds1 in vertebrates have not been observed yet, probably due to lack of good reagents for staining these proteins in vivo.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in current knowledge with a speculative explanation.

claim: It remains poorly understood how polarized distribution of Fat and Ds is established, and how it is coordinated between neighboring cells.
source: It remains poorly understood how polarized distribution of Fat and Ds is established, and how it is coordinated between neighboring cells.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in current knowledge.

claim: Models without feedback propose that observed gradients of Ds and Fj are sufficient to explain the asymmetric distribution of Fat-Ds complexes.
source: Models without feedback propose that observed gradients of Ds and Fj are sufficient to explain the asymmetric distribution of Fat-Ds complexes (Casal et al., 2006; Lawrence et al., 2008; Strutt, 2009; Hale et al., 2015; Abley et al., 2013; Axelrod and Tomlin, 2011).
evidence: This is stated as a description of existing models supported by citations.

claim: Models without feedback cannot explain how relatively small differences in Ds and Fj expression between neighboring cells can lead to strongly polarized membrane distributions.
source: However, these models cannot explain how relatively small differences in Ds and Fj expression between neighboring cells can lead to strongly polarized membrane distributions.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of gradient-only models.

claim: Models that include localized feedback mechanisms can solve the problem of amplifying small differences in expression.
source: This problem is solved by models that include localized feedback mechanisms, where we define 'localized' to mean a feedback at the level of protein complexes within the cell boundary, to distinguish it from transcriptional feedback or tissue scale feedbacks.
evidence: This is stated as an advantage of feedback models.

claim: Localized feedback models have been previously proposed to explain polarity in the core pathway, where the localized feedbacks are mediated by the cytoplasmic proteins Prickle and Dishevelled.
source: Such models have been previously proposed to explain polarity in the core pathway, where the localized feedbacks are mediated by the cytoplasmic proteins Prickle and Dishevelled (Amonlirdviman et al., 2005; Le Garrec et al., 2006; Fischer et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: No localized feedbacks were identified for the Fat-Ds pathway prior to this study.
source: However, no such feedbacks were identified for the Fat-Ds pathway.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in current knowledge.

claim: Two localized feedback mechanisms can be distinguished: a self-enhancing feedback and a mutual inhibition feedback.
source: In principle, two localized feedback mechanisms can be distinguished: (1) a self-enhancing feedback that promotes the formation of additional Ft-Ds complexes in the same direction of existing Ft-Ds complexes, and (2) a mutual inhibition feedback between complexes in opposite direction (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as a theoretical framework and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Mathematical modeling predicts that models with both feedbacks can amplify small differences in expression and create strongly polarized cell boundaries.
source: Mathematical modeling predicts that models with both feedbacks can amplify small differences in expression and create strongly polarized cell boundaries (Mani et al., 2013; Burak and Shraiman, 2009).
evidence: This is stated as a prediction from mathematical models supported by citations.

claim: A model with a self-enhancing feedback alone would lead to roughly equal numbers of opposing complexes.
source: Intuitively, a model with a self-enhancing feedback alone would lead to roughly equal numbers of opposing complexes, whereas a model with mutual inhibition feedback alone would remove pairs of opposing complexes and leave only the small excess of the dominant complex type.
evidence: This is stated as an intuitive explanation of model predictions.

claim: A model with mutual inhibition feedback alone would remove pairs of opposing complexes and leave only the small excess of the dominant complex type.
source: Intuitively, a model with a self-enhancing feedback alone would lead to roughly equal numbers of opposing complexes, whereas a model with mutual inhibition feedback alone would remove pairs of opposing complexes and leave only the small excess of the dominant complex type.
evidence: This is stated as an intuitive explanation of model predictions.

claim: The combination of both feedbacks together leads to strong accumulation of complexes in one direction.
source: The combination of both feedbacks together leads to strong accumulation of complexes in one direction.
evidence: This is stated as an intuitive explanation of model predictions.

claim: Models predict that polarity can emerge spontaneously once threshold levels of Ft and Ds are reached, even in the absence of external gradients.
source: Somewhat less intuitive is the prediction of these models that polarity can emerge spontaneously once threshold levels of Ft and Ds are reached, even in the absence of external gradients (Mani et al., 2013; Burak and Shraiman, 2009).
evidence: This is stated as a prediction from mathematical models supported by citations.

claim: Models for PCP based on the core pathway are equivalent to mutual inhibition feedback and do not require self-enhancing feedback.
source: We note that models for PCP based on the core pathway are equivalent to mutual inhibition feedback described above and do not require self-enhancing feedback.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison between different PCP models.

claim: HEK293 stable cell lines expressing Fat4-citrine and Ds1-mCherry were generated.
source: We generated HEK293 stable cell lines expressing Fat4-citrine under a constitutive CMV promoter (HEK-Fat4-citrine) and Ds1-mCherry under a doxycycline inducible promoter (HEK-Ds1-mCherry).
evidence: This is stated as a method and result in the Results section.

claim: Western blotting confirmed that Fat4-citrine and Ds1-mCherry fusion proteins were expressed and showed the expected molecular bands at ~500 kDa for Fat4-citrine and ~320 kDa for Ds1-mCherry.
source: Western blotting confirmed that these fusion proteins were expressed and showed the expected molecular bands at ~500 kDa for Fat4-citrine and ~320 kDa for Ds1-mCherry (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by Western blot data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Co-culture experiments revealed strong accumulation of Fat4-citrine and Ds1-mCherry at heterotypic junctions.
source: Consistent with the existing evidence for exclusively heterotypic interactions, these co-culture experiments revealed strong accumulation of Fat4-citrine and Ds1-mCherry at heterotypic junctions (yellow arrows in Figure 1D–F)
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by images in Figure 1D-F.

claim: No accumulation was observed in homotypic junctions or in monoculture experiments of either cell line.
source: while no accumulation was observed in homotypic junctions (white arrows in Figure 1D) or in monoculture experiment of either cell line (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B–C).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by images in Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B-C.

claim: Similar accumulation was observed in co-culture experiments of MCF7 cells expressing the same fusion constructs.
source: Similar accumulation was observed in co-culture experiments of MCF7 cells expressing the same fusion constructs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by images in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Ds1-mCherry trans-endocytoses into the Fat4-citrine cells as evident from numerous vesicles containing both Ds1-mCherry and Fat4-Citrine.
source: Surprisingly, we also found that Ds1-mCherry trans-endocytoses into the Fat4-citrine cells as evident from numerous vesicles containing both Ds1-mCherry and Fat4-Citrine (white triangles in insets Figure 1D–F, see also yellow vesicles in Figures 3 and 4).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by images in Figure 1D-F.

claim: No trans-endocytosis of Fat4-Citrine into the Ds1-mCherry cells is observed.
source: No trans-endocytosis of Fat4-Citrine into the Ds1-mCherry cells is observed.
evidence: This is stated as a result based on observations in the images.

claim: This observation is the first evidence for the presence of transendocytosis in Fat-Dachsous pathway.
source: This observation is the first evidence for the presence of transendocytosis in Fat-Dachsous pathway.
evidence: This is stated as a novel finding.

claim: Cells with accumulating boundaries generally express higher levels of either Fat4 or Ds1.
source: We found that cells with accumulating boundaries generally express higher levels of either Fat4 or Ds1 (Figure 2E–F, solid vs. dashed lines, 20 hr time point).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by distributions shown in Figure 2E-F.

claim: Even with long induction times not all Fat4-Ds1 boundaries exhibit accumulation.
source: We note that even with long induction times not all Fat4-Ds1 boundaries exhibit accumulation.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: There is a clear separation between 'accumulating boundaries' and 'non-accumulating boundaries' indicating that accumulation occurs when both Fat4-citrine and Ds1-mCherry are expressed above a certain threshold level.
source: We observed a clear separation between 'accumulating boundaries' (yellow dots in Figure 2H) and 'non-accumulating boundaries' (boundaries without accumulation) (purple dots in Figure 2H) indicating that accumulation occurs when both Fat4-citrine and Ds1-mCherry are expressed above a certain threshold level.
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by the 2D distributions in Figure 2H.

claim: While the fraction of boundaries exhibiting accumulation increased with induction time, the separation between the two populations (i.e the threshold levels) remained almost the same.
source: Note that, while the fraction of boundaries exhibiting accumulation increased with induction time (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C, Figure 2—figure supplement 2D), the separation between the two populations (i.e the threshold levels) remained almost the same (dashed lines Figure 2H).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by data in Figure 2H and supplementary figures.

claim: Such a behavior is expected from a localized feedback model exhibiting bistability.
source: Such a behavior is expected from a localized feedback model exhibiting bistability.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the observed behavior.

claim: Most Ds1-mCherry is localized on the cell membrane, even in the absence of Fat4 expressing cells.
source: We note that most Ds1-mCherry is localized on the cell membrane, even in the absence of Fat4 expressing cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–C)
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by images in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: The measured total and membrane Ds1 levels are proportional.
source: and that the measured total and membrane Ds1 levels are proportional, justifying the use of total Ds1-mCherry as a measure of the relevant Ds1 level in the cell.
evidence: This is stated as a result that justifies a methodological choice.

claim: The fluorescence of both Fat4 and Ds1 proteins exhibit a threshold response at the boundary.
source: The fluorescence of both proteins exhibit a threshold response (black dashed line).
evidence: This is stated as a result and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Ds1-mCherry on the boundary continues to increase faster than the total Ds1 (i.e. in a non-linear fashion) for several hours after accumulation starts.
source: Furthermore, Ds1-mCherry on the boundary continues to increase faster than the total Ds1 (i.e. in a non-linear fashion) for several hours after accumulation starts (Figure 3—figure supplement 1F), consistent with a threshold response.
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The population snapshot experiments and the single cell time lapse movies strongly support a non-linear threshold response of Fat4-Ds1 complexes to the levels of Fat4 and Ds1.
source: Taken together, the population snapshot experiments (Figure 2) and the single cell time lapse movies (Figure 3) strongly support a non-linear threshold response of Fat4-Ds1 complexes to the levels of Fat4 and Ds1.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the combined data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Fat4 and Ds1 fluorescence at the accumulating boundary are proportional as the boundary is formed.
source: Analysis of the three movies described above (Figure 3C and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B–C) showed that Fat4 and Ds1 fluorescence at the accumulating boundary are proportional as the boundary is formed (spanning over two orders of magnitude in fluorescence) (Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D–E).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by data in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D-E.

claim: Analysis of snapshots from 31 boundaries showed a high degree of correlation (ρ = 0.989) over two orders of magnitudes in fluorescence.
source: Similar results were obtained by analyzing snapshots from 31 boundaries showing, a high degree of correlation (ρ = 0.989) over two orders of magnitudes in fluorescence (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by data in Figure 3E.

claim: The linear relation between the accumulation on both sides of the boundary indicates the formation of Fat4-Ds1 complexes with a fixed stoichiometric ratio.
source: This linear relation between the accumulation on both sides of the boundary indicates the formation of Fat4-Ds1 complexes with a fixed stoichiometric ratio.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the proportionality data.

claim: Cadherins can interact cooperatively across the cell boundary to promote cell adhesion.
source: It has been previously shown that cadherins can interact cooperatively across the cell boundary to promote cell adhesion (Chen et al., 2005; Zhang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Stabilization of Fat4-Ds1 complexes, possibly through clustering, can be an underlying mechanism for the self-enhancing feedback.
source: We therefore hypothesized that stabilization of Fat4-Ds1 complexes, possibly through clustering, can be an underlying mechanism for the self-enhancing feedback.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on prior knowledge about cadherins.

claim: Increased stability of Ft-Ds complexes was recently observed in localized puncta on cell boundaries in Drosophila.
source: Consistent with this idea, increased stability of Ft-Ds complexes was recently observed in localized puncta on cell boundaries in Drosophila (Hale et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Analysis of the recovery profile over time showed very slow recovery time (>25 min) on the accumulating boundary, reflecting the extremely low turnover and membrane dynamics of Fat4-Ds1 complexes.
source: Analysis of the recovery profile over time showed very slow recovery time (>25 min) on the accumulating boundary (see boundary on kymograph in Figure 4B), reflecting the extremely low turnover and membrane dynamics of Fat4-Ds1 complexes.
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by FRAP data in Figure 4A-B.

claim: Both Fat4-citrine and Ds1-mCherry exhibited very fast recovery compared to the Fat4-Ds1 complexes, of the order of a few seconds.
source: Both Fat4-citrine and Ds1-mCherry exhibited very fast recovery compared to the Fat4-Ds1 complexes, of the order of a few seconds (Figure 4B and D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by FRAP-TIRF data in Figure 4C-D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The mean diffusion coefficient of Fat4-Ds1 complexes is more than two orders of magnitude smaller than that of unbound Fat4 and Ds1.
source: We found that the mean diffusion coefficient of Fat4-Ds1 complexes is more than two orders of magnitude smaller than that of unbound Fat4 and Ds1 (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The mean exchange rate of Fat4-Ds1 complexes are significantly smaller than those of the unbound Fat4 and Ds1.
source: Similarly, the mean exchange rate of Fat4-Ds1 complexes are significantly smaller than those of the unbound Fat4 and Ds1 (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Complexes formed on the boundary between cells show extremely high stability compared to unbound Fat4 and Ds1.
source: Hence, complexes formed on the boundary between cells show extremely high stability compared to unbound Fat4 and Ds1.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the FRAP data.

claim: Accumulation of N-cad-GFP complexes on the cell boundary exhibited significantly slower dynamics than unbound N-cad-GFP.
source: Similar to the results with Fat4 and Ds1, we found that accumulation of N-cad-GFP complexes on the cell boundary exhibited significantly slower dynamics than unbound N-cad-GFP (Figure 4E–F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C–F).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by FRAP data in Figure 4E-F and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C-F.

claim: The slower dynamics of N-cadherin complexes is consistent with cooperative binding and enhanced stabilization of complexes at the boundary as previously observed for E-cadherin.
source: This result is consistent with cooperative binding and enhanced stabilization of complexes at the boundary as previously observed for E-cadherin (de Beco et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the N-cadherin data supported by a citation.

claim: These results support a model where stabilization of Fat4-Ds1 complexes via clustering serves as a mechanism for localized self-enhancing feedback.
source: Overall, these results support a model where stabilization of Fat4-Ds1 complexes via clustering serves as a mechanism for localized self-enhancing feedback.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the FRAP data.

claim: Unbound Fat4 exhibited significantly faster membrane diffusion than unbound Ds1 despite having a significantly higher molecular weight (500 KDa vs 320 KDa).
source: Finally, we also note that unbound Fat4 exhibited significantly faster membrane diffusion than unbound Ds1 (Figure 4E) despite having a significantly higher molecular weight (500 KDa vs 320 KDa).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the FRAP data in Figure 4E.

claim: Either Ds1 diffusion is somehow inhibited compared to Fat4, or the surface dynamics of Fat4 are enhanced through active transport processes.
source: This suggests that either Ds1 diffusion is somehow inhibited compared to Fat4, or that the surface dynamics of Fat4 are enhanced through active transport processes.
evidence: This is stated as a speculative interpretation of the diffusion data.

claim: Previous work on Drosophila Ft and Ds showed that Ft-Ds complexes form puncta along the cell boundaries.
source: Previous work on Drosophila Ft and Ds showed that Ft-Ds complexes form puncta along the cell boundaries (Hale et al., 2015; Brittle et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Unlike the Drosophila case, but consistent with a previous report in mammalian cells, we mostly observe continuous accumulation along the boundary.
source: Unlike the Drosophila case, but consistent with a previous report (Ishiuchi et al., 2009) in mammalian cells, we mostly observe continuous accumulation along the boundary.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by a citation.

claim: A spatial gap between the peak in red fluorescence (Ds1-mCherry) and the peak in green fluorescence (Fat4-citrine) along the boundary was observed.
source: However, surprisingly, we observed a spatial gap between the peak in red fluorescence (Ds1-mCherry) and the peak in green fluorescence (Fat4-citrine) along the boundary (Figure 5A–C).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by images in Figure 5A-C.

claim: Rainbows were apparent in most boundaries exhibiting accumulation in both HEK293 and MCF7 cells.
source: Rainbows were apparent in most boundaries exhibiting accumulation in both HEK293 and MCF7 cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–H).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by images in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-H.

claim: The shift between red and green fluorescence is not due to chromatic aberration.
source: This shift is not due to chromatic aberration, as images of cells taken with fluorescent beads show clear rainbows even after the chromatic aberration was corrected (Figure 5—figure supplement 1I–N).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by control experiments in Figure 5—figure supplement 1I-N.

claim: Different boundaries in the same picture and even the same cell (when both Fat4 and Ds1 are co-expressed) can exhibit oppositely directed rainbows.
source: Furthermore, we observed that different boundaries in the same picture and even the same cell (when both Fat4 and Ds1 are co-expressed) can exhibit oppositely directed rainbows (see Figure 6B).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by images in Figure 6B.

claim: A similar shift was observed in images taken in super resolution STED microscopy.
source: A similar shift was observed in images taken in super resolution STED microscopy (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–H).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by STED images in Figure 5—figure supplement 1E-H.

claim: Quantitative analysis of 61 boundaries revealed a relatively tight distribution of gaps with mean and standard deviation of 116 ± 63 nm.
source: Quantitative analysis of 61 boundaries revealed a relatively tight distribution of gaps with mean and standard deviation of 116 ± 63 nm (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by the distribution in Figure 5D.

claim: Such a gap between the c-termini of Fat4 and Ds1 is consistent with the length of Fat4 and Ds1 bound to each other in an extended linear form.
source: Such a gap between the c-termini of Fat4 and Ds1 (where the fluorophores are fused to) is consistent with the length of Fat4 and Ds1 bound to each other in an extended linear form.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the gap measurements.

claim: The length of a cadherin ectodomain is 4.5 nm.
source: Given that the length of a cadherin ectodomain is 4.5 nm (Leckband and Prakasam, 2016)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Upon induction of Ds1-mCherry expression we observed clear accumulation of Fat4-citrine and Ds1-mCherry on the boundary between cells expressing both proteins.
source: Upon induction of Ds1-mCherry expression we observed clear accumulation of Fat4-citrine and Ds1-mCherry on the boundary between cells (Figure 6B), similar to the accumulation observed in co-culture of Fat4-citrine and Ds1-mCherry cells (Figure 1D–F).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by images in Figure 6B.

claim: Analysis of high resolution images revealed rainbows similar to the ones observed in co-culture experiments.
source: Analysis of high resolution images (Figure 6C) revealed rainbows similar to the ones observed in co-culture experiments (Figure 5).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by images in Figure 6C.

claim: The observed rainbows show that even in cells expressing both Fat4-citrine and Ds1-mCherry, there is a strong bias in the direction of complex formation on any given cell-cell boundary.
source: The observed rainbows show that even in cells expressing both Fat4-citrine and Ds1-mCherry, there is a strong bias in the direction of complex formation on any given cell-cell boundary.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the rainbow observations.

claim: We generally do not see domains of opposite polarity within single boundaries suggesting that complexes on cell boundaries align in a coordinated manner.
source: Furthermore, we generally do not see domains of opposite polarity within single boundaries suggesting that complexes on cell boundaries align in a coordinated manner.
evidence: This is stated as an observation and interpretation.

claim: This observation is consistent with mutual inhibition feedback between complexes and suggests that direct interaction between opposing complexes is sufficient for generating polarity.
source: This observation is consistent with mutual inhibition feedback between complexes and suggests that direct interaction between opposing complexes is sufficient for generating polarity.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the coordinated alignment observation.

claim: The direction of polarity can differ between boundaries of the same cell.
source: Interestingly, we see that the direction of polarity, i.e., the direction from green to red in the rainbow (black arrow in Figure 6D), can differ between boundaries of the same cell (see, for example, boundaries 2, 3, and 4, in Figure 6B–D).
evidence: This is stated as an observation and supported by images in Figure 6B-D.

claim: This behavior is different from the long range polarization of Ft-Ds observed in Drosophila wing and larvae.
source: This behavior is different from the long range polarization of Ft-Ds observed in Drosophila wing and larvae (Lawrence et al., 2008; Brittle et al., 2010; Rogulja et al., 2008; Aigouy et al., 2010)
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to in vivo observations supported by citations.

claim: The localized polarity observed in the cell culture system is reminiscent of polarity reversal within the same cell recently observed in Drosophila larvae denticles.
source: but is reminiscent of polarity reversal within the same cell recently observed in Drosophila larvae denticles (Rovira et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to in vivo observations supported by a citation.

claim: When the expression gradients of Fat4 and Ds1 are opposed, the polarity aligns with both the Ds1 and Fat4 gradients.
source: We found that when the expression gradients of Fat4 and Ds1 are opposed (such as in boundaries 1,2, and 4 in Figure 6D) the polarity aligns with both the Ds1 and Fat4 gradients.
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by analysis shown in Figure 6D-E.

claim: Boundary accumulation of Ds1 occurs on the side of the cell with higher Ds1 expression.
source: Namely, that boundary accumulation of Ds1 occurs on the side of the cell with higher Ds1 expression, and conversely, boundary accumulation of Fat4 occurs on the side of the cell with higher Fat4 expression.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the gradient analysis.

claim: Boundary accumulation of Fat4 occurs on the side of the cell with higher Fat4 expression.
source: Namely, that boundary accumulation of Ds1 occurs on the side of the cell with higher Ds1 expression, and conversely, boundary accumulation of Fat4 occurs on the side of the cell with higher Fat4 expression.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the gradient analysis.

claim: In situations where both expression gradients are aligned, the direction of polarity can align either with the Fat4 gradient or with the Ds1 gradient.
source: However, in situations where both expression gradients are aligned (such as in boundary 3 in Figure 6D) we found that the direction of polarity can align either with the Fat4 gradient or with the Ds1 gradient.
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: If Fat4 and Ds1 expression gradients are opposed, then the polarity almost always aligned with the direction of both gradients (36 out of 39 boundaries).
source: Repeating this analysis on 107 boundaries (Figure 6E) indeed showed that if Fat4 and Ds1 expression gradients are opposed, then the polarity almost always aligned with the direction of both gradients (bottom pie chart in Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by the pie chart in Figure 6E.

claim: When Ds1 and Fat4 expression gradients were aligned, the polarity aligned with the Ds1 gradient in 33 out of 68 boundaries and with the Fat4 gradient in 27 out of 68 boundaries.
source: On the other hand, when Ds1 and Fat4 expression gradients were aligned (top pie chart in Figure 6E) we got almost equal number of boundaries aligned with Ds1 gradient (33 out of 68) and boundaries aligned with the Fat4 gradient (27 out 68).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by the pie chart in Figure 6E.

claim: This result is consistent with a situation where the polarity is either controlled by the Ds1 expression gradient or controlled by the Fat4 expression gradient, depending which of the two is dominant.
source: This result is consistent with a situation where the polarity is either controlled by the Ds1 expression gradient or controlled by the Fat4 expression gradient, depending which of the two is dominant.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the gradient alignment data.

claim: Live imaging showed that the rainbow feature emerged in the direction of the Ds1 expression gradient that existed before boundary accumulation occurred.
source: The filmstrip from such a movie (Figure 6—figure supplement 1) indeed showed that the rainbow feature emerged in the direction of the Ds1 expression gradient that existed before bundary accumulation occured (no significant Fat4 expression gradient is observed in this movie).
evidence: This is stated as a result and supported by the movie analysis in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: These observations support a picture where localized polarization of Fat4-Ds1 complexes in cell culture is biased by local gradients generated by cell-to-cell variability.
source: Overall, these observations support a picture where localized polarization of Fat4-Ds1 complexes in cell culture is biased by local gradients generated by cell-to-cell variability.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the gradient analysis.

claim: The results provide direct evidence that localized feedbacks on Fat4-Ds1 complexes can give rise to PCP.
source: In this work, we have adopted a synthetic biology approach to planar cell polarity and reconstituted Fat4-Ds1 PCP in a cell culture system to elucidate the basic mechanisms underlying polarity establishment.
evidence: This is stated as the main conclusion in the Discussion.

claim: Large scale snapshot analysis and live cell imaging of single pairs show that accumulation of complexes at the boundary exhibits a threshold response to increasing levels of Ds1 - a hallmark of positive feedback.
source: Large scale snapshot analysis (Figure 2) and live cell imaging of single pairs (Figure 3) show that accumulation of complexes at the boundary exhibits a threshold response to increasing levels of Ds1 - a hallmark of positive feedback.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the data in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: This is the first direct observation of a positive feedback loop in a PCP system.
source: This is the first direct observation of a positive feedback loop in a PCP system.
evidence: This is stated as a novel finding in the Discussion.

claim: Evidence for mutual inhibition between opposing complexes is provided by the finding that strong polarization is consistently found in cells expressing both Fat4 and Ds1, even in the absence of a strong expression gradient in either of the proteins.
source: Evidence for the second class of localized feedback, the mutual inhibition between opposing complexes, is provided by our finding that strong polarization is consistently found in cells expressing both Fat4 and Ds1, even in the absence of a strong expression gradient in either of the proteins (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the data in Figure 6.

claim: The strong polarization and inferred presence of both feedbacks in a minimal synthetic system make it plausible that no other proteins specific to this pathway are involved in the feedback.
source: The strong polarization and inferred presence of both feedbacks in a minimal synthetic system make it plausible that no other proteins specific to this pathway are involved in the feedback, and favor simple mechanisms that rely on direct interactions between the heterotypic complexes.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the synthetic system results.

claim: The self-enhancing feedback could at least in part rely on enhanced stability of complexes, possibly through cluster formation.
source: This observation suggests that the self-enhancing feedback could at least in part rely on enhanced stability of complexes, possibly through cluster formation.
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the FRAP data.

claim: Enhanced stability of clusters was shown to occur with other cadherin such as E-cadherin.
source: Such enhanced stability of clusters was shown to occur with other cadherin such as E-cadherin (Zhang et al., 2009; de Beco et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: FRAP analysis of Drosophila Ft/Ds in wing disk junctions also showed enhanced stability on boundary puncta compared to other boundary regions.
source: Furthermore, FRAP analysis of Drosophila Ft/Ds in wing disk junctions also showed enhanced stability on boundary puncta compared to other boundary regions (Hale et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Enhanced stability may not be the only mechanism contributing to localized feedbacks.
source: Enhanced stability may not be the only mechanism contributing to localized feedbacks.
evidence: This is stated as a caveat in the Discussion.

claim: In addition to stabilizing complexes, clusters could also catalyze their formation by acting as a 'diffusion trap', as has also been suggested for E-Cadherin.
source: For example, in addition to stabilizing complexes, clusters could also catalyze their formation by acting as a 'diffusion trap', as has also been suggested for E-Cadherin (Wu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as a speculative mechanism supported by a citation.

claim: Work in Drosophila has implicated directional trafficking and feedbacks through cytoplasmic PCP components as other potential mechanisms for localized feedbacks.
source: Moreover, work in Drosophila has implicated directional trafficking (Matis et al., 2014) and feedbacks through cytoplasmic PCP components (Amonlirdviman et al., 2005) as other potential mechanisms for localized feedbacks.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The extreme stability of Fat4-Ds1 complexes may make it hard for the cells to change their initial polarity, for example to respond to cell divisions or morphogenetic processes.
source: One potential difficulty with the extreme stability of Fat4-Ds1 complexes is that it may be hard for the cells to change their initial polarity, for example to respond to cell divisions or morphogenetic processes.
evidence: This is stated as a potential issue in the Discussion.

claim: The observed trans-endocytosis of Ds1 into the Fat4 cell may serve as a way to quickly remodel boundaries in spite of their slow turnover by removing large fragments of boundaries with otherwise stable Fat4-Ds1 complexes.
source: Interestingly, the observed trans-endocytosis of Ds1 into the Fat4 cell (Figure 1D–F) may serve as a way to quickly remodel boundaries in spite of their slow turnover by removing large fragments of boundaries with otherwise stable Fat4-Ds1 complexes.
evidence: This is stated as a speculative interpretation of the trans-endocytosis observation.

claim: A recent study suggested that Fat4 and Ds1 fold into a compact structure to fit into intercellular gaps.
source: A recent study, however, suggested that Fat4 and Ds1 fold into a compact structure to fit into intercellular gaps (Tsukasaki et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: It is unclear whether the seemingly contradictory observations about Fat4-Ds1 structure are due to different methodologies or different cellular contexts.
source: It is unclear whether these seemingly contradictory observations are due to different methodologies or different cellular contexts.
evidence: This is stated as an acknowledgment of uncertainty.

claim: The synthetic system shows that expression of Fat4 and Ds1 is sufficient to generate polarized boundaries.
source: Hence, our in vitro setup shows that expression of Fat4 and Ds1 is sufficient to generate polarized boundaries.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the co-expression experiments.

claim: Unlike in vivo tissues where the direction of polarity is coordinated over extended regions, the direction of polarity of each boundary in the in vitro assay seems to be independent of the polarity of nearby boundaries.
source: Unlike in vivo tissues where the direction of polarity is coordinated over extended regions, the direction of polarity of each boundary in our in vitro assay seems to be independent of the polarity of nearby boundaries.
evidence: This is stated as an observation comparing in vitro to in vivo.

claim: The difference between in vitro and in vivo polarity coordination is possibly due to the relatively large cell-to-cell variability in the expression of Fat4 and Ds1 in cell culture.
source: It is possible that this difference is due to the relatively large cell-to-cell variability in the expression of Fat4 and Ds1 in cell culture.
evidence: This is stated as a speculative explanation.

claim: Cell-to-cell variability can lead to local effective gradients of Fat4 and Ds1 biasing the direction of polarity in each boundary.
source: This variability can lead to local effective gradients of Fat4 and Ds1 biasing the direction of polarity in each boundary.
evidence: This is stated as a speculative explanation.

claim: The situation in cell culture is reminiscent of the disordered organization of denticles in Drosophila larvae which was attributed to variability in Ds expression.
source: This situation is reminiscent of the disordered organization of denticles in Drosophila larvae which was attributed to variability in Ds expression (Rovira et al., 2015; Saavedra et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a comparison to in vivo observations supported by citations.

claim: For the unambiguous situation of opposing Fat4 and Ds1 gradients, the polarity (determined independently by the 'rainbow' feature) aligns with the local gradients.
source: Analysis of the direction of Fat4 and Ds1 gradients across each boundary indeed shows that for the unambiguous situation of opposing Fat4 and Ds1 gradients, the polarity (determined independently by the 'rainbow' feature) aligns with the local gradients.
evidence: This is stated as a result from the gradient analysis.

claim: For the case where gradients are incompatible (i.e. pointing in the same direction), the polarity may be determined by either the Fat4 or the Ds1 gradients, depending which one is more dominant.
source: For the case where gradients are incompatible (i.e. pointing in the same direction), the polarity may be determined by either the Fat4 or the Ds1 gradients, depending which one is more dominant (e.g. which gradient is stronger).
evidence: This is stated as a result from the gradient analysis.

claim: The results and conclusions provide a general framework for how complex local interactions between membrane proteins can induce tissue level organization.
source: Our results and conclusions are not limited to the understanding of Fat-Ds signaling but provide a general framework for how complex local interactions between membrane proteins can induce tissue level organization.
evidence: This is stated as a broader implication in the Discussion.
